description: Lamb Ouzi is a magnificent Middle Eastern dish featuring succulent, slow-roasted lamb, often served atop aromatic rice with nuts and spices. This whole slow-roasted version promises a tender, fall-off-the-bone experience bursting with rich, savory flavors. It is a true centerpiece, perfect for special gatherings and family feasts.

instructions.title: Prepare the Lamb
instructions.text: Pat the lamb leg or shoulder dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make several deep incisions all over the lamb. Season generously with salt, pepper, and 1 tablespoon of the mixed spices, rubbing it into the cuts. Set aside to marinate while you prepare the stuffing.

instructions.title: Prepare the Rice Stuffing
instructions.text: In a large pan, heat 1 tablespoon of oil or ghee over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the ground lamb or beef, breaking it up with a spoon, and cook until browned. Drain any excess fat. Stir in 1 cup of rinsed basmati rice, 1 tablespoon of mixed spices, salt, and pepper. Add 2 cups of broth, bay leaves, and cinnamon stick. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes until the rice is partially cooked. Stir in green peas.

instructions.title: Stuff and Sear the Lamb
instructions.text: Carefully stuff the partially cooked rice mixture into the incisions made in the lamb. You can also create a pocket by carefully lifting the skin or making a deeper cut in a thicker part of the lamb. Secure the lamb with butchers twine if necessary to hold the stuffing. In a large roasting pan, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil or ghee over high heat (or sear in a separate large pan). Sear the lamb on all sides until nicely browned. This step adds depth of flavor and color.

instructions.title: Slow Roast the Lamb
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 325F (160C). Place the seared lamb in the roasting pan. Pour the remaining 4 cups of chicken or beef broth into the pan around the lamb. Cover the roasting pan tightly with foil. Roast in the preheated oven for 4-5 hours, or until the lamb is fork-tender and easily pulls away from the bone. Baste occasionally with the pan juices.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ouzi Rice
instructions.text: While the lamb is roasting during its last hour, prepare the main Ouzi rice. In a large pot, heat 1 tablespoon of oil or ghee. Add 2 cups of rinsed basmati rice, a pinch of salt, and 4 cups of broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until all liquid is absorbed and rice is fluffy. Let it rest for 5 minutes off the heat.

instructions.title: Assemble and Serve
instructions.text: Once the lamb is cooked, remove it from the oven and let it rest, covered, for at least 15-20 minutes before carving. This allows the juices to redistribute. Fluff the Ouzi rice with a fork and arrange it on a large serving platter. Carefully place the whole slow-roasted lamb on top of the rice. Garnish generously with toasted pine nuts, almond slivers, and freshly chopped parsley or mint. Serve immediately with any pan juices on the side.

tips: For maximum flavor, marinate the lamb overnight in the refrigerator with the spices and a splash of olive oil before roasting.
Do not overcook the rice for the stuffing; it should be partially cooked to finish cooking within the lamb without becoming mushy.
Resting the lamb after roasting is crucial. It ensures the meat remains juicy and tender when carved, preventing dryness.
article:
Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted: A Middle Eastern Feast for the Senses

Imagine a dish so grand, so fragrant, and so utterly delicious that it becomes the undisputed star of any celebration. In the rich tapestry of Middle Eastern cuisine, Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted holds precisely that esteemed position. More than just a meal, it’s an experience – a symbol of hospitality, generosity, and culinary artistry. If you're searching for an impressive centerpiece that will leave your guests talking for weeks, look no further than an authentic Lamb Ouzi recipe. This isn't just about cooking lamb; it's about transforming humble ingredients into a spectacular feast, slow-roasted to perfection until the meat is fall-off-the-bone tender and infused with a symphony of aromatic spices.

## What is Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted?

Lamb Ouzi, often simply called Ouzi, is a revered dish across the Levant and Gulf regions, particularly popular in countries like Syria, Jordan, Lebanon, and Iraq. While the term "Ouzi" can sometimes refer to individual pastries filled with spiced meat and rice, the grandest and most traditional rendition involves a whole or a significant cut of lamb (like a leg or shoulder) that has been slow-roasted for hours. This Lamb Ouzi recipe focuses on the majestic whole slow-roasted lamb, which is then typically served atop a generous bed of aromatic, spiced Basmati rice studded with peas, carrots, and toasted nuts, and sometimes even ground meat.

The magic of Lamb Ouzi lies in its patient preparation. The lamb is marinated extensively, absorbing a complex blend of spices that penetrate deep into the meat during the long, gentle cooking process. The slow roasting breaks down tough connective tissues, rendering the lamb incredibly succulent, tender, and moist, with a rich, savory flavor that is simply unparalleled. It’s a dish designed for sharing, usually presented on a massive platter, inviting diners to gather around and partake in a communal culinary celebration. It embodies the essence of Middle Eastern hospitality, promising abundance and warmth.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting an unforgettable Lamb Ouzi recipe begins with selecting the finest ingredients. Here’s what you’ll need to assemble this magnificent feast:

For the Lamb:
*   1 whole bone-in lamb leg or shoulder (approx. 5-7 lbs / 2.5-3.5 kg)
*   1/2 cup olive oil
*   1/4 cup lemon juice
*   10-12 cloves garlic, minced
*   2 tablespoons salt
*   1 tablespoon black pepper
*   1 tablespoon ground cumin
*   1 tablespoon ground coriander
*   1 tablespoon sweet paprika
*   1 teaspoon ground turmeric
*   1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
*   1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom
*   1/2 teaspoon ground cloves
*   1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
*   Fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs (optional, for cavity or roasting pan)

For the Aromatic Rice:
*   3 cups Basmati rice, rinsed until water runs clear
*   2 tablespoons olive oil or ghee
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   3-4 cloves garlic, minced
*   1 lb (450g) ground lamb or beef (optional, but traditional in some versions)
*   1 cup frozen peas
*   1/2 cup chopped carrots (optional)
*   4 cups lamb or chicken stock
*   1 tablespoon salt
*   1 teaspoon black pepper
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
*   1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom

For Garnish:
*   1/2 cup toasted pine nuts
*   1/2 cup toasted slivered almonds
*   Fresh parsley, chopped

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Following this detailed Lamb Ouzi recipe will guide you to culinary success, ensuring a dish that impresses in both flavor and presentation.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb (Marinate):**
    *   Pat the lamb leg/shoulder completely dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, score the fatty side of the lamb in a diamond pattern, about 1/2 inch deep, without cutting into the meat itself. This helps the marinade penetrate and the fat render.
    *   In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, salt, pepper, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and nutmeg.
    *   Generously rub the marinade all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the scored areas. For best results, place the lamb in a large roasting pan, cover, and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, or preferably overnight. Allow it to come to room temperature for about an hour before roasting.

2.  **Slow Roast the Lamb:**
    *   Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C).
    *   Place the marinated lamb in a sturdy roasting pan. You can add a cup of water or stock to the bottom of the pan to create steam and prevent drying. Add rosemary and thyme sprigs if desired.
    *   Cover the roasting pan tightly with aluminum foil.
    *   Roast for 4-5 hours, or until the lamb is incredibly tender and easily pulls away from the bone. The exact time will depend on the size of your lamb and your oven. For the last 30-45 minutes, remove the foil to allow the exterior to brown slightly. An internal temperature of 190-200°F (88-93°C) indicates fall-apart tenderness.
    *   Once cooked, remove the lamb from the oven, transfer it to a cutting board, tent it loosely with foil, and let it rest for at least 30 minutes before carving. This is crucial for juicy meat.

3.  **Prepare the Aromatic Rice:**
    *   While the lamb is resting, prepare the rice. Heat olive oil or ghee in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
    *   Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
    *   If using ground meat, add it now and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned. Drain any excess fat.
    *   Stir in the rinsed Basmati rice, salt, pepper, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, and cardamom. Toast the rice and spices for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
    *   Pour in the lamb or chicken stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15 minutes.
    *   Remove from heat and let it steam, still covered, for another 10 minutes.
    *   Fluff the rice with a fork, then gently fold in the frozen peas and chopped carrots (if using). The residual heat will cook the peas and carrots.

4.  **Assemble and Serve:**
    *   On a large serving platter, spread out the aromatic rice.
    *   Carve the slow-roasted lamb into large, rustic pieces, or if it's falling off the bone, simply arrange it attractively over the rice.
    *   Garnish generously with toasted pine nuts, slivered almonds, and fresh chopped parsley.
    *   Serve immediately.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Mastering a Lamb Ouzi recipe requires patience and attention to detail. These pro tips will elevate your dish from good to extraordinary:

*   **Marination is Key:** Do not skip the overnight marination. The longer the lamb sits in the spice blend, the deeper and more complex its flavor will be.
*   **Low and Slow is the Way to Go:** Resist the urge to crank up the heat. The gentle, prolonged roasting at a low temperature is what guarantees melt-in-your-mouth tenderness.
*   **Rest Your Meat:** After roasting, allowing the lamb to rest for at least 30 minutes (or even longer for a larger cut) redistributes the juices, resulting in a more succulent and flavorful meat.
*   **Flavorful Stock for Rice:** Use high-quality lamb or chicken stock for your rice. This adds another layer of depth and ensures the rice is as aromatic and flavorful as the lamb itself.
*   **Toast Your Nuts:** Toasting the pine nuts and almonds before garnishing brings out their inherent sweetness and nuttiness, adding a delightful crunch and aroma.
*   **Score the Lamb:** Scoring the fat allows the marinade to penetrate better and helps the fat render beautifully, contributing to a crispy exterior if you choose to finish it under the broiler briefly.
*   **Don't Overcook the Rice:** Basmati rice cooks quickly. Follow the instructions carefully to avoid mushy rice. A slight al dente texture is ideal as it will absorb more flavors from the lamb juices.

## Serving Suggestions

Presenting your finished Lamb Ouzi recipe is an art in itself. It's designed to be the centerpiece, but a few complementary sides can enhance the experience:

*   **Yogurt Sauce:** A simple, refreshing yogurt sauce (like labneh or plain Greek yogurt thinned with a little water, mixed with minced garlic, dried mint, and a squeeze of lemon) provides a lovely contrast to the richness of the lamb.
*   **Fresh Salads:** Crisp, vibrant salads like Fattoush (with toasted pita bread, sumac, and fresh vegetables) or Tabbouleh (parsley and bulgur wheat salad) offer a refreshing counterpoint.
*   **Pickles:** Assorted Middle Eastern pickles (like pickled turnips, cucumbers, or olives) add a tangy, briny element that cuts through the richness.
*   **Warm Flatbread:** Serve with warm pita bread or markouk bread for scooping up the delicious lamb and rice.
*   **Roasted Vegetables:** A side of simply roasted vegetables like asparagus, green beans, or bell peppers can add color and nutrition.

## Variations and Substitutions

While this Lamb Ouzi recipe is a classic, there's always room for personal touches and adaptations:

*   **Different Cuts of Lamb:** If a whole leg or shoulder is too much, you can use smaller bone-in lamb cuts like shanks or even a boneless roast, adjusting cooking times accordingly. The slow-roasting principle remains the same.
*   **Rice Fillings:** Experiment with the rice. Add dried cranberries or raisins for a touch of sweetness, or different vegetables like diced bell peppers or chickpeas for added texture and flavor.
*   **Spice Profile:** Adjust the spices to your preference. Increase the chili flakes for a bit of heat, or add a touch more cinnamon or cardamom for a warmer, sweeter aroma. Some regions might include dried lime (loomi) in the rice for a tangy depth.
*   **Stuffed Lamb (Traditional Ouzi):** In some very traditional and elaborate preparations, a deboned whole lamb is actually stuffed with the spiced rice and then roasted or even pit-roasted. This is a highly skilled undertaking, and for most home cooks, serving the lamb over the rice is the more practical and equally delicious approach.
*   **Ouzi Rolls:** A popular variation, especially as an appetizer or smaller meal, involves wrapping the spiced rice and ground lamb mixture in phyllo pastry to create individual Ouzi rolls, which are then baked until golden and crispy. While delicious, it's a different dish from the whole slow-roasted version.

Whether you're celebrating a special occasion or simply want to create an unforgettable meal for your loved ones, this Lamb Ouzi recipe promises an unforgettable dining experience. Its rich history, incredible flavors, and impressive presentation make it a true masterpiece of Middle Eastern culinary tradition. Enjoy the process, savor the aromas, and delight in the sheer joy of sharing this magnificent feast.
